news.title: AI Voice-Cloning Scam: That 'Urgent Call from Grandma' Is a Fake
news.excerpt: Scammers clone voices with just 3 seconds of audio — a TikTok, a voicemail, an Instagram Reel. They call pretending to be a grandchild in jail needing bail money. Hang up. Call the real person on a known number. No real emergency demands gift cards, crypto, or instant wire transfers. Agree on a family safe word NOW.

news.title: FTC Warns: Fake CAPTCHA Scams Hijack Your Computer
news.excerpt: Scammers use fake CAPTCHAs that tell you to press Windows+R, paste, and Enter — this runs malicious code. Real CAPTCHAs never ask for keyboard commands. Close the tab immediately if a verification asks you to open Run or paste anything.

news.title: 16 Billion Stolen Passwords: Check If Yours Are Out There
news.excerpt: A massive database of 16 billion stolen usernames and passwords is circulating. Check haveibeenpwned.com and change reused passwords immediately. Use a password manager like Bitwarden.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — Tech Support Scams: The Phone Call That Costs You Everything
news.excerpt: Scammers pose as Microsoft Support, claim they detected a virus, and demand remote access. Once inside they steal files, drain bank accounts, or lock you out. Microsoft, Apple, and Google NEVER call you out of the blue. Hang up immediately. If worried about your computer, call someone you trust or bring it to the shop. Tech support phone scams cost Americans over $500M last year — average loss $400–$600.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — Update Firefox & Chrome Now — Exploit Code Is Public
news.excerpt: Mozilla confirmed public exploit code now exists for two critical Firefox flaws (CVE-2026-15718 and CVE-2026-15719); Chrome also shipped emergency fixes for 15 bugs, two critical. Fully close Firefox to install 152.0.6, and in Chrome click Menu → Help → About Google Chrome to force the update now — don't wait for the slow auto-rollout.

news.title: 🔴 ALERT — New "Avalon" Malware Framework Is Spreading Through Phishing Emails
news.excerpt: A dangerous new malware framework named Avalon is spreading through plain-looking phishing emails, packaged with CrownX ransomware. Once opened it can steal passwords, move through your home network, and lock your files for ransom. Never open attachments or click links in unexpected emails — type the web address in yourself.

posts.title: Windows 11 File Explorer Now Deletes Large Files Significantly Faster
posts.summary: Update to Windows 11 July 2026 update (KB5101650) via Windows Update to get the faster File Explorer deletion.
posts.truth: Lake City customers bring in laptops choking on old downloads and temp folders. Deleting thousands of small files used to freeze File Explorer for minutes. Microsoft finally fixed the underlying I/O path in the July update — large folder deletions now finish in seconds instead of minutes. I still see machines with 50+ GB in Downloads folders because people don't know how to clean them.
posts.cta: Bring your device to ONYX SYSTEMS or call (386) 755-7772 for help.

posts.title: Turn On Windows Storage Sense to Automatically Free 5–50 GB Monthly
posts.summary: Open Settings → System → Storage → Storage Sense → Turn on. Set cleanup schedule to "During low free disk space" or "Monthly." Configure cleanup schedules for temp files, Recycle Bin (30 days), and Downloads folder (60 days).
posts.truth: Lake City FL customers bring in laptops with 5 GB free on a 256 GB drive. They don't know Storage Sense exists. It's built into Windows 11 — no download, no cost, no ads. I've seen it reclaim 40 GB on a single laptop in one run. Most people never touch Storage settings until the red bar appears.

posts.title: Microsoft Fixes 622 Security Flaws — Biggest Patch Tuesday Ever
posts.summary: July 2026 Patch Tuesday addresses 622 vulnerabilities including 6 critical remote code execution flaws and starts mandatory Kerberos RC4 enforcement. Open Settings → Windows Update → Check for updates, install, and restart. Network admins: test Kerberos AES compatibility.
posts.truth: This is the largest Microsoft security update on record. The Kerberos change alone affects every Windows domain. ONYX SYSTEMS can help test and deploy these updates safely.

posts.title: Storage Sense — Windows' Free Cleanup Tool Runs Automatically
posts.summary: Press Start and type "Storage Sense", turn it On. Click Configure Storage Sense and choose how often to run (daily/weekly/monthly). Set Delete files in Recycle Bin after to 30 days. Set Delete files in Downloads folder after to 60 days (or Never if you keep installers). Automatically frees 10-50 GB of temp files and junk — no extra software needed. Works on Windows 10 and 11.
posts.truth: Customers pay for "PC tune-up" software that does exactly what Storage Sense does for free. ONYX SYSTEMS shows you how to enable it in 2 minutes.

posts.title: Windows has a free ransomware shield built in — turn it on in 30 seconds
posts.summary: Open Windows Security (press Start and type "Windows Security"). Click Virus & threat protection, then Manage ransomware protection. Turn on Controlled Folder Access. Click Protected folders and add your Documents, Pictures, and Desktop folders. Only programs you approve can save files there — ransomware gets blocked automatically.
posts.truth: People pay for "ransomware protection" software that just wraps this free Windows feature. Microsoft built it into Windows Defender years ago — it works, but it's OFF by default because some old programs break. I turn it on for every customer and add the 5-6 apps they actually use. Zero ransomware infections in three years. Included with any tune-up.

posts.title: Firefox now lets you keep work, banking, and shopping separate — free, built-in, no add-ons needed
posts.summary: Update to Firefox 153 or newer (free at mozilla.org/firefox). Click the menu, choose New Container Tab, and pick Work, Personal, Banking, or Shopping. Each container has its own cookies and logins — your work Google can't see your personal YouTube history. It's the only browser that actually separates them at the engine level.
posts.truth: Most people use Chrome profiles or incognito and think they're separated. They're not — Google still links them by IP and fingerprint. Firefox Containers is the only mainstream browser feature that actually isolates cookie jars at the engine level. I run four containers daily and it's the single best free privacy upgrade. I set this up for customers in 10 minutes.

posts.title: Check your SSD health free — and why your Windows warnings lie
posts.summary: On Windows, install CrystalDiskInfo free from crystalmark.info. It shows your SSD's real health — percentage used, temperature, hours powered on. Most drives warn at 80% life used; I've seen drives die at 95% with zero Windows warnings. Check it once a month.
posts.truth: Windows' "drive is healthy" means almost nothing — it only checks the filesystem, not the NAND wear. I've pulled SMART data off drives Windows called perfect that had 2% spare blocks left. The honest answer: if smartctl shows "Percentage Used" over 80, budget for a replacement this quarter.
